what: All parry sounds are short single transients with no low body and no sustain. Perfect parry (anvil.land p1.8 + trident.hit, then a quiet amethyst/bell ring at tick 2): falls 10 dB in 0.14 s and 20 dB in 0.24 s; the reference clang+ring holds for 0.55 s / 1.02 s. Its 100-400 ms level is 11 dB below the reference and its ring partials are 12 dB weaker. Tier 2 (chain.hit p1.7 + amethyst.hit p1.9) and tier 1 (chain.hit p1.25) are 50-90 ms mid-band clinks at 0.75-1.3 kHz. They are 5-6 dB quieter than the loudest other combat sound within 1 s, so they are masked. The reference guard tink is bright (3.7 / 1.9 / 2.3 kHz partials) and lasts about 0.46 s. There is no swing whoosh in the last 0.3 s before contact (the 1.5-12 kHz band is at -64 dBFS, i.e. silence); the reference has a pitched swoosh sweep 0.35-0.2 s before contact.

measured.method: 5 ms hop STFT, bands 20-150 / 150-500 / 500-1500 / 1500-12000 Hz, dBFS mean power; medians over events
measured.tier2_tier1_same_family: both are block.chain.hit at different pitch; tier 2 adds amethyst.hit. By ear they are near-identical short clicks

likely_cause: data/rlk/function/player/def/fx/p1_at, p2_at, p3_at, p3_star: one-shot transient vanilla sounds at volume 0.5-0.9 with no low layer and no sustained ring layer; the ring (p3_star) is at 0.35-0.9 volume and pitched high. Nothing plays the boss swing.

what: Every dodge is the same 3-block dash in 3 ticks (dash_dir: dashMoveT 3, 1 block per tick = 1.67 avatar heights in 0.15 s), whether an attack is coming or not, with the avatar laid flat in a horizontal "superman" pose for about 12 frames. About 95 dash-sound matches in the fight (template match on the dash sound). The reference has no such dash. With nothing incoming the character hardly moves: a twist with the sword thrown out, under 0.3 body heights. With an attack incoming it is a quick upright back-step of about 1.5-2.2 body heights. With a direction held it is a low lunge-step. A second press is a cartwheel.

measured.reference: see the measured block of T3-03

likely_cause: data/rlk/function/player/dash_dir.mcfunction (fixed dashMoveT 3, step x10); char/motion/dash clip leans the body to horizontal

what: Measurements of the reference dodge.mp4 that an implementer can copy. Travel is floor-compensated: the character position minus the floor flow, divided by the on-screen body height (105-145 px at half resolution). Depth toward or away from the camera is foreshortened, so depth figures are +-40 %. A: plain dodge, no attack, no direction (4.5 s, f258-293). She stays in place, under 0.3 bh. The torso twists and the sword is flung out sideways (f268-276). About 12 frames, no smear. B: dodge against an incoming attack (1.6 s, 2.8 s, 15.4 s; f108-113, f164-206, f918-951). A straight back-step away from the enemy, toward the camera: about 1.9 bh (2.8 s) and 2.2 bh (15.4 s). The move itself is fast, 5-12 frames, with a smear. She stays upright with the legs apart and lands with the arms spread wide; ready about 18-25 frames after the press, settled by about 35. C: directional dodge (8.4 s and 14.0 s; f500-540, f836-876). A low lunge-step in the input direction (sideways here), deep forward lean, trailing leg straight, sword low behind. About 1.4 bh (14.0 s) and up to 2.6 bh (8.4 s, probably including a run-in). 20-25 frames of movement, standing again about 40 frames after the start. D: double dodge (second press 0.55-0.6 s after the first; 10.0-11.3 s, f596-672; log "SHIFT->SHIFT 더블 닷지"). The first press is a back-step (about 1.0 bh left and back, f600-632). The second is a sideways cartwheel: about 360 deg around the camera-forward axis, f644-664 (20 frames), inverted with the feet up at f652-656, landing f664-668, about 1.3 screen bh further back, ready by f672. E: the reference normal dodge has no slow motion, tint or vignette, and no distinct sound above the room tone.

backstep_vs_attack.pose: upright, legs apart, arms spread on landing

directional.pose: low lunge, deep lean, trailing leg, sword low

measured.caveat: Only one clear in-place example. Whether "no attack" or "enemy too close" triggers it is an interpretation. The coordinator said the author wants this set to replace the long dash.

what: In real time our perfect dodge matches the reference within 2-4 frames (landing at +57..+60 frames in both). It feels slow because nothing moves for long stretches. (1) It opens with the 3-block flat dash (+0..+16). (2) Then 20 frames of "slow motion" in which the avatar barely moves; in PD4 the avatar-region frame difference drops from 20-30 to 1-14 (frames 10104-10122). The reference keeps her moving at 1/3 speed (arching back, arms up) and moves the camera (13-15 deg tilt or a 90 deg whip). (3) The flip begins only 0.65-0.68 s after the press. (4) The flip is a rigid rotation of the blocky avatar: 0->90 deg in about 2 frames, held inverted about 5 frames, legs together (no split), landing in a T-pose. (5) Whole sequence about 64-67 frames to tint-off and 81 frames to the beat end, against our normal dodge of 9 frames (7-9x longer). (6) The camera never moves. It reads as a handspring done by a mannequin. Arc height and travel are small: it plays in place after the dash.

measured.PD2_PD3_165.9-167.1s: back-to-back; tint continuous 9968-10150; the camera was inside her model 9958-9980, so not timed

likely_cause: player/def/beat/d/clock (slow 6-14, flip 14-21, end 27) with the stand-in rig clip char/motion/beat/dodge: the clip holds the pose during the slow ticks and runs the flip as a rigid rotation; the dash runs before the beat and the camera is untouched

what: Sounds around parries that mask them: (1) the dash sound (wind_charge.wind_burst p1.4 + breeze.slide p1.5) at -20..-30 dBFS total, louder than the perfect parry (-29) and the tier ticks (-31/-32); (2) the boss parry cue (bell.use + beacon.power_select: 656 Hz, 2.0 kHz, 4.0 kHz, about 80 ms) 0.37 s before the hit, at the same level as the parry sound itself (-32 dBFS); (3) player skill and impact sounds with a strong low end (20-150 Hz up to -21 dBFS); (4) in P2 a steady tone around 300-400 Hz raises the bed by about 8-10 dB.

When she is close (the gauntlet ghost next to the avatar), the slash crescent is a huge translucent pink sheet near the camera, about 35-45 % of the frame, lasting about 22 frames (10680-10702, 9238-9262), longer than the about-6-tick target. Its plane against the blade could not be measured at this distance. Away from the camera the scalloped pink fan stands beside her for about 25 frames (10019-10043).
likely_cause: crescent scale is not limited by camera distance; lifetime counted in world ticks, and the freeze extends it
